### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 322cf9068f143f39cbfbc7527294db24f01cd649` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7971e1cd249c0b76b62e85886cf2b9d072a4f3d3` — the merge of head `8ec800e416727581b828060a616db4ef9d45feca` into base `322cf9068f143f39cbfbc7527294db24f01cd649`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7971e1cd249c0b76b62e85886cf2b9d072a4f3d3 && git checkout 7971e1cd249c0b76b62e85886cf2b9d072a4f3d3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 322cf9068f143f39cbfbc7527294db24f01cd649 8ec800e416727581b828060a616db4ef9d45feca && git checkout -B drift-repro 322cf9068f143f39cbfbc7527294db24f01cd649 && git merge --no-ff 8ec800e416727581b828060a616db4ef9d45feca

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 322cf9068f143f39cbfbc7527294db24f01cd649
```

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Enforcement is unchanged.** Every hunk of permission-evaluator.ts read: (a) the `ConditionedFieldEntry` interface gains `supersededBy: string[]` and its docblock, a type-only change; (b) the docblock of `conditionedFieldEntries` gains one sentence; (c) inside `conditionedFieldEntries` one `const supersededBy = superuserFieldVote(permissionSets, objectName)?.editable ? this.superuserBypassSets(objectName, permissionSets, { bit: 'modify' }) : []` and one `supersededBy: [...supersededBy]` on the pushed entry. `getFieldPermissions`, `superuserBypassSets`, `hasSuperuserReadBypass`, `hasSuperuserWriteBypass`, `checkObjectPermission` and `resolveObjectPermission` are untouched. `conditionedFieldEntries` has exactly two callers in the tree at this head, both in `explainObjectPass` §4 of explain-engine.ts (the agent's sets and, under D10, the delegator's); no gate, middleware, masker or `/auth/me/permissions` merge reads it, and the two functions it now calls are pure reads (`holdsSuperuserBypass` over `objects[name] || objects['*']`). The attribution comes from `superuserBypassSets(…, { bit: 'modify' })`, which is `holdsSuperuserBypass(ps, objectName, 'modify')` per set, the very predicate `superuserFieldVote` returns `editable: true` on; so the list is non-empty exactly when the vote is editable, and the sentence can never name a set the merge did not read, nor read a vote no set is named for. This is the shape `superuserBypassSets`' own docblock prescribes for the record level ("the layer's `contributors` attribution and the enforcement decision are the same list"). No extraction was needed: the seam the delta asked for already lives in core since #29387, and both readers now call it. The ablation disabled the vote read in `conditionedFieldEntries` and the Modify All case went red, which is the right anchor for "the report reads the vote, not a restatement". **Right**.
3. **View All supersedes nothing here, correctly.** `superuserFieldVote` returns `{ readable: true, editable: false }` for a set that holds `viewAllRecords` only, so `?.editable` is false and `supersededBy` is `[]`. In `getFieldPermissions` that vote sets `readable = true` on the fields the merge holds and leaves `editable` as the per-entry votes left it; a conditioned entry's read bit is already `true` (`permission.zod.ts` refuses `readable: false` beside a `when`, the refinement at the end of `FieldPermissionSchema`), and `fieldPermissionVote` under `unjudged` grants no edit, so for a View All holder the conditioned entry's edit lock still binds per row exactly as before. The second `[#29610]` case pins the old sentence for an `hr_auditor` set with `allowRead` + `viewAllRecords` and `not.toContain('superseded')`. The docblock on the new member states this reason in the same words. **Right**, and the dev's measurement (the write gate refuses the field for the View All caller) agrees with the code.
4. **D10.** The agent's entries are judged against `sets` and the delegator's against `delegatorSets`, each call computing its own `supersededBy`; the enforcement for a delegated call intersects the two masks, so a delegator's conditioned lock binds when only the agent holds the vote, and the report now says so (the entry lands in `binding`). The superseding set names in the sentence are the union over both principals' superseded entries; each entry still names its declaring set. **Right**.
5. **Wording.** Superseded entries move into a sentence of their own, `N row-conditioned field permission(s) are superseded by the Modify All Data field vote [SETS], which votes every field editable on every row, so the lock binds on no row: [...]`, the verb and bracketed-set form the record-level sharing attribution already uses (`Superseded by the View/Modify All Data bypass [SETS] — see the vama_bypass layer.`); binding entries keep the existing sentence with their own count. The delta's "annotate or drop, whichever matches how the report already words other overrides" is met by annotate, with the precedent named. One cosmetic reading, not a fix: for an entry authored `editable: true` with a `when`, the superseded sentence prints `(editable when …)` followed by "so the lock binds on no row"; the "lock" there is the row-blind one (no edit grant off the matched rows), which the vote does remove, so the sentence is true, only less literal for that shape. **Right**.
6. **The wire and the SDK are untouched.** The explain report crosses HTTP as `ExplainDecisionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts`), whose fls layer is `{ layer, verdict, detail: z.string(), contributors[] }`; `ConditionedFieldEntry` never leaves the engine, and only the prose of `detail` changes. No spec file, no `packages/client*`, no `ui/**` moves. **Right**.
7. **Where `supersededBy` does land: on the package's published type graph.** `@objectstack/plugin-security` publishes (`package.json` has no `private`, `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`, `exports["."]` → `dist/index.d.mts`), and `src/index.ts` re-exports the `PermissionEvaluator` class and the `ExplainEngineDeps` type (`evaluator: PermissionEvaluator`). `ConditionedFieldEntry` is not re-exported by name, but it is reachable from the entry through the return type of the public method `conditionedFieldEntries`, and by the repo's own definition of the public surface (execution-duties: 「公开面 = 包构建后的入口声明所达 … 所达 = 再导出名,加经其 props、参数与返回类型可达的每个类型」) a type reachable through a return type is on it. The member is required (`string[]`, never optional), so a consumer that hands `explainAccess` a structurally typed evaluator of its own must now return it; nothing in this repo does (the only constructor of the shape is the evaluator; `makeDeps` in the explain tests uses `new PermissionEvaluator()`), and the one `toEqual` pin that spells the shape is the forced edit in ③. The ruling on what this means for `Clause-②` is in ②.
8. **The forced test edit is honest.** `security-plugin.test.ts` `[#25866] conditionedFieldEntries lists the row-conditioned entries of the object, as authored` builds `makePermSet('hr', {}, {...})` with an empty `objects` map, so no set holds either super-user bit and `supersededBy: []` is the true value of the new member for that fixture; the pin is exact `toEqual`, so the member had to be spelled, and nothing else in the case moves (the two conditioned entries, their `set`, `when` and `editable` are as before). Declared as a deviation in the report and named in the PR body with its reason. **Right**.
9. **Files outside the declared surface.** The claim's surface is explain-engine.ts, "the shared vote seam in plugin-security if an extraction is needed", explain-engine.test.ts and a changeset. permission-evaluator.ts is where `conditionedFieldEntries`, the seam the explain engine reads, lives, and the change there is the seam change the claim's clause anticipates (no extraction, because the vote already lives in core; the seam is widened by one output member instead). security-plugin.test.ts is the forced edit of ①.8. No `packages/spec/**`, no `ui/**`. **Accepted**, both named.

The three cases drive the real `PermissionEvaluator` through `explainAccess`, not a stub, so the vote they exercise is core's. **Right**.
